To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a SiC-based power module, in conjunction with a dual-interleaved hard-switching converter topology, results in a 40% reduction in total losses, and a 27% reduction in overall system weight, compared with an IGBT-based system, whilst maintaining the same power rating and output voltage.

the use of SiC power modules in the design of a 50 kW, 200 A dc-dc converter has enabled a reduction in the total weight and losses of 27% and 40%, respectively, and a power density of more than 10 kW/kg.
the SiC converter has a higher efficiency than the IGBT converter and a lower weight, resulting in higher power density.

the SiC power module is a viable alternative to the IGBT-based power module for high-power applications.
